title: A Static for the Vector
premise: When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the Halcyon System, cargo hauler Odile Iversen—a clone of a murdered detective—is the only witness whose implanted memory survives the event, because the flicker was a weaponized memory-wipe that rewrote the system's archives. The wipe conceals the Kettle Station massacre, which the original Odile investigated before his death, and the fleet's fragile truce expires in ninety days. Odile must rebuild the case from physical residue, unreliable clone-memory, and the testimony of people whose minds were edited, while the Vector Combine—the power that committed the massacre—hunts him to destroy the last proof. In the end, Odile broadcasts the massacre's true record during the truce's final hour, sacrificing his ship and nearly his identity, forcing the Combine into a negotiated surrender but leaving him unsure which memories are truly his own.
about_author: Ansel Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard container ships before turning to fiction, and his work obsesses over the static between transmitted signals and the truths they fail to carry. He lives in Lagos and Accra by turns and claims he writes only at night, when the satellites are loudest.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Odile Iversen hauls ore through contested orbits, haunted by a murder case he inherited in his donor's memories. Gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds; his ship survives, but his nav-computer's logs are scrambled and every station goes silent. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread as he realizes the flicker was not an accident.

chapters.title: The Case That Was Never Closed
chapters.summary: Docking at Waypoint Nine, Odile finds his inherited case files—the Kettle Station massacre—have been purged from every archive he can reach, including his own ship's backup. Only the memories cloned into his head still contain the investigation. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being the sole container of a forbidden truth.

chapters.title: Truce in Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Commander Sefa Adeyemi warns Odile that the armistice between the Fleet and the Vector Combine expires in ninety days, and both sides are hunting the cause of the flicker. She half-suspects him already. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: institutional caution wrestling with a gut feeling that Odile matters.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Hold
chapters.summary: Odile discovers a stowaway: Iyo Renk, a Kettle Station survivor whose mind was wiped but who instinctively flees Combine ships. Her fragmented terror corroborates the massacre in Odile's cloned memories. POV: Iyo. Emotional beat: two broken memory-keepers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Odile interrogates his own inherited memories in a neural dive, mapping the original detective's final investigation: a Combine labor reclamation on Kettle Station that killed four hundred people and was erased in twelve hours. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grief for a man whose mind he wears like an inherited coat.

chapters.title: The Vector's Smile
chapters.summary: Combine executive Loras Venn contacts Odile with a courteous offer: a new ship and a clean registry in exchange for his neural archive. The threat beneath the courtesy is unmistakable. POV: Venn. Emotional beat: the seductive, corrupting confidence of institutional power that has never been refused.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Odile and Iyo jump to the wreck of the original's last ship, drifting in a debris field. They recover a physical evidence core—pre-wipe recordings of Kettle Station—just as a Combine salvage crew arrives. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: triumph curdling instantly into flight.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: A silent chase through a nebula shoal; Odile burns his transponder and navigates by dead reckoning while Iyo's wiped memory surfaces in flashes that help him evade pursuit patterns she shouldn't remember. POV: Iyo. Emotional beat: the body remembering what the mind was forced to forget.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefa offers Odile Fleet protection in exchange for the evidence core—but he learns the Fleet plans to use it as leverage in truce negotiations, not justice. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: her loyalty to the Fleet cracking against what she knows is right.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Static
chapters.summary: A quiet interlude at a smugglers' haven: Odile confronts the question of whether his love of hauling, his habits, his griefs are his or the original's. Iyo argues that choosing what to keep is what makes a self. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the theme of identity made intimate and unresolved.

chapters.title: Kettle Station, Standing
chapters.summary: They reach Kettle Station itself—repopulated, repainted, its inhabitants given new implanted histories. A station elder's child draws a massacre she was never told about. POV: Iyo. Emotional beat: horror at how thoroughly power can rewrite a place and call it mercy.

chapters.title: The Editor
chapters.summary: They capture Dr. Halvane, the Combine memory-architect who designed the wipe, hiding on Kettle under a new name. She reveals the nine-second flicker was a system-wide edit—and that a second, larger edit is scheduled before the truce expires. POV: Halvane. Emotional beat: a technician's amoral pride beginning to rot into guilt.

chapters.title: Proof That Isn't
chapters.summary: The Fleet's forensic board rules Odile's evidence core inadmissible: in a post-wipe system, no record is provably authentic. Sefa is ordered to detain him. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: the law revealed as another instrument of the powerful.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Waypoint Nine
chapters.summary: A trusted smuggler ally sells Odile's location to Venn. Iyo is captured; the evidence core is seized; Odile escapes with nothing but Halvane's testimony and a burn scar. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: rage and the temptation to simply run and keep hauling forever.

chapters.title: What Halvane Buried
chapters.summary: Halvane, wracked by conscience, reveals she kept a private key: a checksum that can authenticate the wiped records against the flicker's own signature, proving the edit happened. POV: Halvane. Emotional beat: the first true act of courage from a lifelong coward.

chapters.title: The Combine's Clock
chapters.summary: Venn accelerates the second wipe to truce-eve; Sefa, ordered to stand down, instead feeds Odile the Fleet's interception schedule—openly committing treason. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: a career officer choosing conscience over institution.

chapters.title: Rescue Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Odile and Halvane infiltrate Combine Station Vesper where Iyo is held and the wipe array is charged. The rescue succeeds at the cost of Halvane's life; she dies transmitting the checksum to Odile's implant. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grief converted directly into resolve.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Truce-eve. The Combine prepares a system-wide second wipe; the Fleet prepares for war; Odile has one ship, one checksum, and hours. He and Iyo plot a broadcast path through the same debris field where the original died. POV: Iyo. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce clarity.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: as the second wipe begins, Odile pilots his dying ship through Combine interdiction and broadcasts the authenticated massacre record—checksummed against the flicker itself—onto every open channel in the system, including the Combine's own fleet displays. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: transcendence; the static finally carrying the signal.

chapters.title: What the Whole System Saw
chapters.summary: Four hundred names, faces, and final hours flood every screen. Combine crews refuse the wipe order; Venn's board turns on him; the truce collapses into surrender negotiations instead of war. POV: Venn. Emotional beat: the architecture of corruption failing all at once.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the Kettle dead are publicly named, Iyo testifies, and Sefa presides over restitution hearings. Odile, shipless, is offered a detective's commission—the original's old job, newly real. He must decide whose life he is living. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the quiet after transmission.

chapters.title: A Static of His Own
chapters.summary: Odile accepts the commission on his own terms, keeping hauling as a second trade, and dives one last time into his cloned memories—not to sort theirs from his, but to choose the whole of it. He signs his own name beneath the original's in the reopened case file. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: identity resolved not as inheritance or originality, but authorship.
